item.title: #3582994: The AI connector silently drops unrecognized input names
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +68/−10 · php +68/−10
  • Diff: 4942ae0
  • Discussion: #3582994 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Tool module's AI connector (tool_ai_connector) used to drop arguments it didn't recognize. A model that misspelled an input name only heard that the input it meant was missing, so it retried with the same wrong key. The connector now reports the unrecognized name, for example numbr: This input is not defined for the tool., and the tool doesn't run. This matches how the MCP bridge and drush tool:run already behaved. A value passed for a locked input is also rejected now, with "This input is locked and cannot be changed." Existing setups may start failing if they pass keys the tool doesn't declare.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: tool_ai_connector is stricter: an argument the tool doesn't declare, or a value for a locked input, now fails the call instead of being ignored.
  • New API: ToolPluginBase::populateValues() is overridden to set every argument.

Technical details

Arguments were being dropped in two places before ToolRunner::run() saw them. One was the ai module's FunctionCallBase::populateValues(), which skips arguments with no context definition. The other was ToolPluginBase::execute(), which forwarded only declared input names. The fix overrides populateValues() in Drupal\tool_ai_connector\Plugin\AiFunctionCall\ToolPluginBase. The override calls setContextValue() for every argument, undoing the __colon__ escaping the way the parent does. execute() now passes every stored value to the runner, with unescapePropertyKeys applied through array_map. The runner's existing validation then produces the "not defined" and "locked" violations, which come back in the structured output with success false and the input schema. The context mirroring step after execution now uses array_intersect_key($values, $definitions), so undeclared and locked names, which have no definition, are skipped there. Kernel tests in ToolPluginBaseStructuredOutputTest cover a misspelled name, an extra name set through setContextValue(), and a locked input.

Upgrade

The issue notes that ai_agents' default_information_tools sets every parameter key from the agent's YAML with setContextValue() and doesn't check the names. An undeclared key in that YAML now fails the call, so remove or correct keys the tool doesn't declare. Callers that pass a value for a locked input must also stop doing so.

item.title: #3583027: tool:info should print declared input examples in the usage line
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +60/−10 · php +60/−10
  • Diff: c1608a7
  • Discussion: #3583027 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

The usage line printed by drush tool:info now uses the first example declared on an input definition instead of a made-up value. Before this, a tool declaring examples: ['Oma'] still showed "word":"example_word" in the usage line, even though the JSON Schema printed just above listed Oma. Inputs with no declared examples keep the generated placeholder values.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In ToolInfoCommand, getExampleValue() now takes the InputDefinitionInterface instead of a data type string. It returns reset($definition->getExamples()) when examples exist. Otherwise, for a ListInputDefinition it returns a one-item list built recursively from getItemDefinition(), so nested lists produce [[1]]. For anything else it uses the existing match on data type. A declared example of 0 is honored, because the check is !== [] rather than a truthiness test. The change applies to both the table and markdown output formats. New tests in ToolInfoCommandTest cover declared examples on example_values_tool (field_tags, 0, ["alpha"]) and list fallbacks on recursive_scalar_transform_tool.

item.title: #3583053: MapAdapter discards default values of nested properties
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +418/−5 · php +418/−5
  • Diff: 4eaacb0
  • Discussion: #3583053 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

Map inputs in the Tool module's configuration forms now show their nested properties' declared default values. Before, the property fields of a map input rendered empty. Each field now shows the stored value if there is one, otherwise the property's declared default. This applies at every level of a nested map. Entity properties inside a map also show the right entity when the value is an entity ID.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

MapAdapter::formElement() now reads the map's current value and calls setValue() on each property's typed data before building its element. It uses the stored value when the key exists, including a stored FALSE. Otherwise it uses the property's declared default. A property stored as NULL stays empty, so a cleared value does not bring the default back. A nested map stored as NULL is built like an empty map, so its own properties show their defaults. A value the property cannot hold throws \InvalidArgumentException, which is caught and the value dropped.

Core MapDataDefinition properties have no default of their own, so EffectiveDataDefinition::copyPropertyDefinitions() now copies the default of each InputDefinitionInterface property into a new EffectiveDataDefinition::DEFAULT_VALUE_SETTING (tool_default_value) setting on the rebuilt definition. Output definitions do not get it. EffectiveDataDefinition is @internal.

EntityAdapter gets a private getEntity() helper. A map property's stored value or default is often an entity ID rather than an entity object, so the helper loads the content entity by ID. It returns NULL for config entity types, IDs that do not load, other value shapes, and definitions with no fixed entity type. The helper result feeds both the target type and #default_value of the autocomplete. New kernel tests cover MapAdapter defaults and EntityAdapter ID handling.

item.title: #3583059: Config entities do not cross a handle boundary
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +441/−30 · php +427/−29 · md +14/−1
  • Diff: 1c8757e
  • Discussion: #3583059 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

Tools can now take and return config entities, such as user roles, through invokers that ask for entity handles, for example an MCP server or the AI connector. Before, the input schema had no type, so a model didn't know what to send. Sending a machine name failed validation. Config entity outputs came out as empty objects. Now these entities cross the boundary as their machine name (for example editor) and the schema says string. An unknown machine name fails the input with a clear error. Content entities still use handles, and invokers without EntitiesAsHandles see no change.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: EntityHandleTransformer gains public isConfigEntityDefinition(), resolveConfigInput() and transformConfigOutput(). New MachineNameNotFoundException implements HandleExceptionInterface.

Technical details

When the invoker has InvokerCapability::EntitiesAsHandles, EntityHandleTransformer::isConfigEntityDefinition() detects an entity:TYPE definition whose entity class implements ConfigEntityInterface. transformInputDefinition() and transformOutputDefinition() turn it into a string definition, with "(pass the machine name of the TYPE)" appended to the description for inputs. The bare entity data type is not covered, because the entity type is needed to load by ID.

On input, EntityHandleTransformSubscriber checks for a config entity definition before the content entity case. It calls resolveConfigInput(), which loads the entity through the type's storage. Non-string values pass through untouched. On output, transformConfigOutput() replaces a config entity with its ID and a hint. The batch path handles lists, either isMultiple() outputs or ListOutputDefinition items. It replaces each config entity with its ID and adds one hint per list, such as "Output roles contains 2 user_role machine name(s)".

An unknown machine name throws the new Drupal\tool\Handle\MachineNameNotFoundException. It is final, extends \RuntimeException and implements HandleExceptionInterface. It is separate from HandleNotFoundException, so a wrong value does not get the advice about handle expiry and ownership. The input violation names the input property. The commit adds a config_entity_tool test tool in tool_test and updates the handle docs.

Upgrade

Code that catches HandleExceptionInterface already covers the new MachineNameNotFoundException. Code that catches HandleNotFoundException specifically will not see unknown machine names, and needs to catch the new class or the interface.

item.title: #3594827: Uninstall deletes every .json file under the results path
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +446/−54 · php +401/−32 · md +45/−22
  • Diff: 67c3cd9
  • Discussion: #3594827 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Two fixes in AI Eval 1.1.x. First, uninstalling the module used to delete every .json file under the configured results path, including files it never wrote when the path pointed at a shared folder. It now removes only its own result files and envelope exports. Second, the Import traces page used to offer a server path option to anyone with operate ai eval. That option now appears only for users with administer ai eval. Operators can still upload a file. The Drush import command is unchanged and has no permission check, so the docs now say to restrict shell access.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Users with only operate ai eval can no longer import traces from a server path. Only administer ai eval can. Forged form posts are rejected.
  • Permission change: The server path source on the Import traces page now requires administer ai eval. Uploads still work with operate ai eval.

Technical details

ai_eval_uninstall() now scans non-recursively. In the results path it matches only /^results-\d{8}-\d{6}\.json$/. In the envelopes/ subfolder it matches only /\.eee\.json$/. It skips anything that is not a regular file, such as a directory with a matching name. A FileException on one delete is caught, so one failure cannot block uninstall. It then tries rmdir() on the envelopes folder, which succeeds only if the folder is empty. The results path itself stays. The default temp folder, used when results_path is empty, is not cleaned, and neither are files written by ai-eval:export-envelope --output-dir.

In TraceImportForm, a new canUseServerPath() checks administer ai eval. Without it, the source radios and server_path field are not built. source becomes a value element fixed to upload, and the upload field's #states visibility is dropped so it always shows. validateForm() also rejects source=path coming from either the form values or the raw user input. This covers forged posts, because the value element would otherwise hide them. It returns one fixed error on source, "You do not have permission to import from a server path. Upload a file instead.", so operators learn nothing about whether a path exists.

The commit also adds kernel tests for uninstall and form validation, a functional test for the operator view and a forged post, and changelog and docs updates. The changelog credits #3594827 for uninstall and #3594821 for the import restriction.

Upgrade

No update steps are needed. If operators who hold only operate ai eval import from server paths, grant them administer ai eval, have an administrator do the import, or use drush ai-eval:import-traces. Uninstall no longer removes .json files in the results path that do not match results-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json or envelopes/*.eee.json. Remove any other leftover files by hand.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 24, 2026
  • Committed: October 30, 2026 (6 days later)

item.title: #3594821: Operators can probe server paths and import JSON from any readable directory
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +446/−54 · php +401/−32 · md +45/−22
  • Diff: 67c3cd9
  • Discussion: #3594821 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The Import traces page no longer offers the server path option to users who only have Operate AI Eval. Previously those users could type any server path. They could learn which paths exist and import JSON from any readable directory. Now only users with Administer AI Eval see that option. Operators can still upload a file. The same change narrows module uninstall. It now deletes only the result and envelope files AI Eval wrote, not every .json file under the configured results path (tracked as #3594827). The Drush import command is unchanged and has no permission check.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Users with only operate ai eval could probe server paths and import JSON from any readable directory through the trace import form. The server path option now requires administer ai eval, enforced in form build and validation.
  • Permission change: Importing from a server path on the Import traces page now requires administer ai eval. File upload still accepts operate ai eval or administer ai eval.

Technical details

TraceImportForm gets a canUseServerPath() check on administer ai eval. Without it, the source radios and server_path field are not built. source becomes a value element fixed to upload, and the upload field's #states visibility dependency is dropped so the field is always visible. validateForm() also rejects a forged post. If the user lacks the permission and either the form value or the raw user input has source set to path, it sets the same fixed error on source, "You do not have permission to import from a server path. Upload a file instead." This runs before any path is checked, so existing, missing and unreadable paths all get the same message and nothing leaks.

ai_eval_uninstall() in ai_eval.install now scans non-recursively. At the top level of results_path it matches /^results-\d{8}-\d{6}\.json$/. In results_path/envelopes it matches /\.eee\.json$/. It skips non-files and catches FileException per file, so one failed delete does not block uninstall. It then tries rmdir() on the envelopes folder, which succeeds only if the folder is empty. The results path, other files, subfolders, the default temp folder and --output-dir exports are left alone. New tests cover the operator-only form, a forged POST, the validation guard and the uninstall patterns. The docs (traces.md and the uninstall notes), the CHANGELOG and the results_path field description are updated. The docs also note that Drush reads any path the shell user can read.

Upgrade

Nothing to run. Operators who relied on the server path option need an administrator to run the import, or they can use drush ai-eval:import-traces. If you want old results files removed on uninstall that don't match results-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json or envelopes/*.eee.json, delete them manually.

Contribution

  • Committed: October 30, 2026 (6 days later)

item.title: #3583098: Make the runner's input errors actionable for agents, and let it be autowired
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +391/−36 · php +388/−35 · yml +2 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: a913c59
  • Discussion: #3583098 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

When a tool run fails on bad input, the error text now tells an agent (or any caller) what to change. An unknown input lists the inputs the tool accepts, a missing required input reads "This input is required.", and a value of the wrong type reads like "This input must be a string." or "This input must be an integer." without extra constraint messages for that input. The ToolRunner class can also now be autowired. Code or tests that match the old messages, such as "This value should not be null.", need updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Input validation message text changed (This input is required., This input must be a string., unknown input lists accepted inputs); NOT_AN_ENTITY_ERROR now also marks a required single entity input left out.
  • New API: ToolRunner is now a service alias for tool.runner, so it can be autowired.

Technical details

In TypedInputsTrait, the unknown-input InputException message now ends with "It takes a, b, c." (or "It takes no inputs."), built from getInputDefinitions(), so locked inputs are not offered. In validateInputValues(), a NULL value on a required input yields a single "This input is required." violation in place of the NotNull detail. For a single (non-multiple) entity input, that violation carries TypedInputsInterface::NOT_AN_ENTITY_ERROR, so drush tool:run still appends its "cannot pass entities" advice. Lists of entities get no code.

In validateInputValue(), primitive typed data now goes through a new validatePrimitiveType() first. It runs only core's PrimitiveType constraint, and skips even that for arrays, because other validators (e.g. Regex via preg_match(), and the URI check via parse_url()) throw on an array. If the type is wrong, it returns one violation worded as the input schema words the type: string, integer, number, true or false, decimal formatted as a string, URI with a scheme, RFC 3339 date-time, YYYY-MM-DD, ISO 8601 duration, or timestamp. The DateOnly and DateTime constraint markers narrow the datetime wording. Other constraints on that input are then not run.

A service alias for ToolRunner pointing at @tool.runner is added to the module's services file. The diff also adds a test tool, quoted_constraint_tool, and a test asserting that a constraint message with quotes stays plain text for text callers after PlainTextOutput::renderFromHtml(). The result message is still escaped once for HTML callers.

Upgrade

Callers or tests that matched the old text need updating, for example:

Invalid input:
recipient: This input is required.

This replaces recipient: This value should not be null. An unknown input now reads nope: This input is not defined for the tool. It takes entity, mode. For advice on entity inputs, match on TypedInputsInterface::NOT_AN_ENTITY_ERROR rather than on message text. You can now type-hint the ToolRunner class in an autowired service.

Contribution

item.title: #3583104: ToolRunner loses the invocation when an output transform throws after execute()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +156/−23 · php +156/−23
  • Diff: e693a70
  • Discussion: #3583104 · 1 contributor · 19 comments

Summary

When a tool had already run but one of its output transform subscribers then threw, the exception escaped ToolRunner::run() and the caller never got the invocation. Invokers such as Drush tool:run and the AI connector recorded the call as if the tool had never run. Now the call comes back as a normal Runtime failure that still reports the tool as executed. The message names only the exception type, and the full error goes to the log.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The catch landed in ToolBase::getFormattedResult(), the alternative the issue mentioned, rather than in ToolRunner::run(). The whole output-transform loop is wrapped in catch (\Throwable $e). The catch logs with Error::logException(). If the raw result is successful, it replaces $this->result with ExecutableResult::failure(ToolMessages::unexpectedFailure($e), $context_values, FailureCategory::Runtime). It then returns a FormattedExecutableResult built from that result. It assigns $this->result directly because setFailureResult() refuses to replace an existing result. Direct callers of getFormattedResult() get the same behavior as the runner.

If the tool had already returned its own failure, that failure is kept, since its reason is more useful than the exception type. Handle exceptions thrown by a transform are also treated as Runtime failures, not Input failures, because the tool has run. The formatted result for the failed call has empty context values, while the raw getResult() still carries the tool's original context values.

In ToolRunner::run() the HandleExceptionInterface catch now covers only a handle exception from a tool's own access check, before execute(). That is still an Input failure. The final \Throwable catch still rethrows when hasExecuted() is TRUE, so it never overwrites an existing result. The ToolInterface docblock now notes that a transform failure replaces a successful raw result with a failure. Kernel tests in ToolRunnerTest cover \RuntimeException, \TypeError and HandleNotFoundException, and the case where the tool's own failure is preserved.

Upgrade

No changes are needed for invokers. eca_tool can drop the README sentence about the executed-then-lost edge case, as noted in the issue.

item.title: #3583105: An unmarked datetime output advertises core's `date` schema but sends the stored datetime
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +103/−33 · php +96/−33 · md +7
  • Diff: b0c273c
  • Discussion: #3583105 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

A Tool module output typed as a datetime but without a DateTime or DateOnly marker used to advertise a date schema while returning the raw stored value, such as 2026-08-01T12:35:07. That value matched neither date nor date-time. Now the schema says the value is either an RFC 3339 date-time or a plain date. Values go out to match: a stored datetime gets a UTC offset, and a bare date stays a date. Tools that want one fixed format should still declare a marker.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: An unmarked datetime_iso8601 output now advertises anyOf date-time or date, and a storage-format value is sent as RFC 3339.

Technical details

The issue offered two options: treat unmarked like DateTime, or advertise no format. The fix is a hybrid. OutputTypeCoercionSubscriber now converts a datetime_iso8601 string in the UTC storage format to RFC 3339 (2026-08-01T12:35:07+00:00) unless the output carries DateOnly. Previously it did this only when DateTime was present. A bare date, or a value that already has an offset, is returned unchanged. A bare date is not promoted to midnight UTC.

In InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer, the branch that was limited to inputs now applies to outputs too. An unmarked datetime gets anyOf: [{format: date-time}, {format: date}] and the description note "An RFC 3339 date-time, or a date alone as YYYY-MM-DD." This matches the input side from #3583005. DateTime and DateOnly outputs keep their single format. For a nullable output, the anyOf branches still allow null, and a test covers that.

Tests: timestamp_output_tool gained unmarked updated_at and due_on outputs, so the schema conformance sweep now covers this case. OutputCoercionMatrixTest gained marked, unmarked, bare date, offset and DateOnly cases. The docs text on output markers was also updated.

Upgrade

Tool authors who return an unmarked datetime_iso8601 value in storage format will now see it sent with a +00:00 offset. To pin a single format, declare a marker on the output:

constraints: ['DateTime' => []],  // advertised as date-time
constraints: ['DateOnly' => []],  // advertised as date, value left as returned

item.title: #3583111: Remove the deprecated normalizer name and legacy adapter alter hook before rc1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +0/−137 · php +0/−130 · yml +0/−7
  • Diff: bbbab3d
  • Discussion: #3583111 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

The Tool module drops two backward-compatibility shims before 1.0.0-rc1. The old ContextDefinitionNormalizer class and its tool.normalizer.context_definition service ID are gone, and so is the old hook_data_type_adapter_info_alter() hook for altering typed data adapters. Custom or contrib code still using the old names will break and must switch to the new ones.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Removed Drupal\tool\Normalizer\ContextDefinitionNormalizer, the tool.normalizer.context_definition service alias, and support for hook_data_type_adapter_info_alter().
  • Deprecation: Completes the removal of shims deprecated in tool 1.0.0-beta4 (adapter alter hook) and 1.0.0-beta12 (normalizer name), as scheduled for rc1.

Technical details

The deleted ContextDefinitionNormalizer was an empty subclass of InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer that only triggered a deprecation. Its deprecated alias in tool.services.yml and ContextDefinitionNormalizerDeprecationTest are removed with it.

In TypedDataAdapterManager, the alterDefinitions() override is deleted. It fired the legacy data_type_adapter_info alter hook before delegating to the parent. The constructor's alterInfo('tool_typed_data_adapter_info') already runs hook_tool_typed_data_adapter_info_alter(), so the new hook is unaffected. Per the issue, Drupal\ai\Utility\ContextDefinitionNormalizer from the ai module is a different class and is not touched.

Upgrade

Replace references to the old normalizer and rename the alter hook implementation:

// Before
\Drupal\tool\Normalizer\ContextDefinitionNormalizer
// service: tool.normalizer.context_definition

// After
\Drupal\tool\Normalizer\InputOutputDefinitionNormalizer
// service: tool.normalizer.input_output_definition

Rename hook_data_type_adapter_info_alter() implementations to hook_tool_typed_data_adapter_info_alter().

item.title: #3583115: `tool:info` and `ToolDefinitionSerializer::normalizeOutputSchema()` return different shapes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +11/−10 · php +8/−9 · md +3/−1
  • Diff: 3e0643d
  • Discussion: #3583115 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

In the Tool module, drush tool:info --format=json now prints a tool's output_schema as a JSON Schema object, the same shape as input_schema, the serializer and the MCP bridge. Before, it printed a bare map of output name to schema, so code written against one form broke on the other. Scripts that parse tool:info output need to read the output names under output_schema.properties.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: drush tool:info --format=json now prints output_schema as {type: object, properties: {...}} instead of a map of output name to schema.

Technical details

ToolInfoCommand::buildSchemas() now calls ToolDefinitionSerializer::normalizeOutputSchema() instead of normalizeOutputDefinitions(), so the printed output_schema matches what the serializer returns. The ?: new \ArrayObject() fallback is gone, since the wrapped schema is never an empty list. For a tool with no outputs the result is {"type":"object","properties":{}}. The separate outputs key is unchanged: one entry per output with type and required. The Drush command docs were updated to describe output_schema as an object schema shaped like input_schema, and ToolInfoCommandTest was updated to match.

Upgrade

Consumers of drush tool:info --format=json should read output schemas from the properties key:

// Before: $data['output_schema']['received']['title']
// After:
$data['output_schema']['properties']['received']['title'];

item.title: #3583121: An input transform or refiner that throws escapes ToolRunner::run(), and Drush and the connector catch only \Exception
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +169/−31 · php +163/−25 · md +5/−5 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 9a67258
  • Discussion: #3583121 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

If an input transform subscriber or a refiner throws before a tool runs, ToolRunner::run() no longer lets the exception escape. An \Error such as a TypeError used to become a fatal at the Drush CLI and abort the whole AI connector batch. A plain \Exception used to reach the user with its raw message. Now the run returns a failed invocation that did not execute, with a Runtime failure message naming only the exception class ("Tool execution failed: TypeError. The full error has been logged."). The detail goes to the site log. drush tool:run reports these failures as execution_failed with that message.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ToolRunner constructor takes a fourth argument, the logger.channel.tool logger; tool.runner service definition updated. ToolRunCommand constructor gains the same logger.
  • New API: ToolMessages::unexpectedFailure(\Throwable $e) builds the type-only failure message.

Technical details

ToolRunner::run() gets a final catch (\Throwable $e) after the HandleExceptionInterface and InputException catches. It logs through Error::logException() and records a FailureCategory::Runtime failure. If a tool was already resolved it uses setFailureResult() and returns ToolInvocation::forTool($tool). If not, it returns ToolInvocation::forFailure(). If the tool hasExecuted(), the throwable is rethrown, so failures after execute() (output transforms) are left to #3583104. The message comes from the new ToolMessages::unexpectedFailure(), and ToolBase::execute() now uses the same helper.

The two in-tree invokers widen their last-resort catch from \Exception to \Throwable. Both log the exception and surface only the type. In ToolRunCommand, a Runtime failure category in the result now maps to RunErrorType::ExecutionFailed. Previously everything that was not Access mapped to InvalidInput. In the Drush output, the earlier "Error running tool '<id>': <message>" form is replaced by the type-only message. The Drush README and RunErrorType docs now describe execution_failed as "a bug in the tool or the site", no longer limited to execute() throwing.

Upgrade

Code that constructs ToolRunner or ToolRunCommand directly must pass the tool logger. The tool.runner service definition already does:

tool.runner:
  class: Drupal\tool\Tool\ToolRunner
  arguments: ['@plugin.manager.tool', '@account_switcher', '@current_user', '@logger.channel.tool']

Scripts that parse drush tool:run --json output may now see error_type: execution_failed for failures in input transforms or refiners, where this used to be a crash or a raw exception message.

item.title: #3586813: Add Box Question and Answer types, and model capability to Decision model infrastructure
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 24 files, +851/−41 · php +765/−24 · md +86/−17
  • Diff: f38c4f4
  • Discussion: #3586813 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Decision operation can now ask a fourth kind of question, a box question, which asks where one described target is in an image. The answer is a box of four edges (top, bottom, left, right) given as fractions of the image size, plus a confidence. Providers opt in by declaring a new DecisionBox capability, which requires image file support. The Decision Explorer shows box answers, including the box in pixels for each uploaded image. This supports the TypeSafe Jev 1.14 box feature described in the issue.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: QuestionFactory and AnswerFactory now accept box. DecisionRequestValidator rejects box questions without an image file with AiBadRequestException. Models without DecisionBox now fail box questions with AiMissingFeatureException instead of an unknown-type error. The shared contract suite image fixtures changed from 1×1 PNG/GIF to 300×300 PNG/JPEG.
  • New API: New BoxQuestion, BoxAnswer, QuestionInterface::TYPE_BOX, DecisionResponse::getBox() and AiModelCapability::DecisionBox (decision_box) for Decision calls.

Technical details

Box is added to the closed set of question types. QuestionInterface::TYPE_BOX and a final BoxQuestion (instructions only, getCriteria() returns NULL) are added. QuestionFactory::fromArray() builds it and throws on any criteria. BoxAnswer validates that every edge and the confidence are finite and in 0 to 1, and that left <= right and top <= bottom. Equal edges are allowed, since transport rounding can collapse a thin box. getBox() returns the edges keyed top, bottom, left, right. toPixels($width, $height) rounds outward (left and top down, right and bottom up), so right and bottom are exclusive as in a crop rectangle. AnswerFactory dispatches box, and DecisionResponse::getBox() behaves like getScore(): it throws AiDecisionRefusedException for a refusal and \UnexpectedValueException for another type.

DecisionRequestValidator maps box questions to AiModelCapability::DecisionBox. A new final check throws AiBadRequestException for a box question when the request has no image files. A model without DecisionBox still gets AiMissingFeatureException first. In DecisionCapabilities, DecisionBox requires DecisionImageFiles and does not count as one of the noul, choice or score types a profile must declare.

In the explorer (DecisionGenerator), box rows show the edges, the confidence and a pixel box per uploaded image, because the explorer cannot tell which image the instructions named. The generated code example uses getBox(). The capability summary substitutes a placeholder image when box questions are present, to avoid a false "needs an image" error. Guardrails are unchanged. Moderation is text-only and stops requests with files, so it stops every box request. The docs (call_decision.md, decision_provider_contract.md, explorer index) are updated. The provider contract suite gets a box request case, malformed-box cases and a box-without-image check. The commit also changes the shared fixture images to a 300×300 PNG and a 300×300 JPEG, because the issue says TypeSafe rejects GIF and images under 256 px per side. The commit also changes a DeepChatLazyLoadTest test to dispatch focusin instead of calling focus(), which is unrelated to the feature.

Upgrade

Provider authors whose model can locate targets in images can declare it, together with image support:

new DecisionCapabilities([
  Capability::DecisionNoul,
  Capability::DecisionImageFiles,
  Capability::DecisionBox,
]);

Return box answers in the normalized shape ['type' => 'box', 'box' => ['top' => 0.25, 'bottom' => 0.82, 'left' => 0.44, 'right' => 0.84], 'confidence' => 0.92]. Adapters that declare DecisionImageFiles now run against 300×300 PNG and JPEG fixtures in the shared contract suite, which replace the 1×1 PNG and GIF. Callers read results with $response->getBox('id').

item.title: #3601413: Install git on the host by default; add --skip-git-install
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +284/−26 · bats +202/−19 · sh +64/−4 · md +12/−3 · 1 +4 · yml +2
  • Diff: 3836e9c
  • Discussion: #3601413 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

The installer now installs git on the host by default, alongside Docker and DDEV. Before this, on a fresh Linux machine --config-url (and remote-config picks or pull) stopped with "requires git, which was not found on this host". The git install is best-effort, so builds that never clone a repo still run if git can't be installed. A new --skip-git-install flag opts out. With that flag, a config fetched from a URL needs git already installed, and the error message names the flag.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New --skip-git-install flag on setup-site; git is now installed on the host by default.

Technical details

A new src/lib/platform/ensure_git.sh adds two functions. ensure_git returns early if git exists or INSTALL_GIT is 0. On Linux it installs git from distro packages (apt-get or dnf, using PKG from linux_detect_distro). On macOS it only warns with an xcode-select --install / brew install git hint. It warns and returns 1 on any failure instead of dying. step_ensure_ddev calls ensure_git || true after _ensure_ddev_cli.

A config URL is cloned before the pipeline reaches step_ensure_ddev. So load_config_url and _git_clone_ref now call require_git, which installs git on demand and dies if it can't. If --skip-git-install was given, require_git dies with a message naming that flag. INSTALL_GIT (default 1, 0 with the flag) is set in setup_site_command.sh next to YOLO, not in apply_cli_flags, so it is already in effect at clone time. The flag is declared in src/bashly.yml, and the generated script, man page and usage docs were regenerated. New bats tests cover the behavior.

Upgrade

To keep the previous behavior of not installing git, pass the new flag:

--skip-git-install

A --config-url or remote-config source then needs git already installed.

item.title: #3578168: Streamed chatbot agent response
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +498/−10 · php +497/−10 · neon +1
  • Diff: 35d0fef
  • Discussion: #3578168 · 3 contributors · 31 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

AI assistants backed by an AI agent now honor streaming output. Before, calling streamedOutput(TRUE) on an agent-backed assistant had no effect, and the whole response came back as one complete message. Now the response comes back as a streamed iterator, as it does for assistants without an agent.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: AgentRunner::runAsAgent() gains an optional trailing bool $streaming = FALSE parameter.

Technical details

AiAssistantApiRunner::process() now passes $this->streaming as a new last argument to AgentRunner::runAsAgent(). When it is set, runAsAgent() calls setStreamedOutput(TRUE) on the ChatInput it gives the agent. If solve() returns a StreamedChatMessageIteratorInterface, the runner wraps it in a ChatOutput and returns it right away. Its normalized value is the iterator itself.

Persisting the agent thread state in the ai_assistant_threads temp store used to happen before solve(). It moved into a private storeAgentState() method. For streamed responses it runs from a callback registered with $response->addCallback(), so state is saved or deleted only once the stream completes. Non-streaming runs call it right after solve(). If the agent is not finished, the state is saved. Otherwise it is deleted.

The commit adds unit tests: AgentRunnerStreamingTest and AiAssistantApiRunnerAgentStreamingTest. The issue's remaining-tasks list also names a check of agents that need several LLM or tool-call loops before the final streamed answer. The diff has no test for that.

Existing callers of runAsAgent() need no change, because the new parameter defaults to FALSE. To stream from code that calls it directly:

$output = $agent_runner->runAsAgent($assistant_id, $chat_history, $defaults, $job_id, FALSE, [], TRUE);

item.title: #3585956: ResourceContentCache reuses the first caller's cache-context variation for every later caller
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +189/−76 · php +167/−56 · md +14/−18 · yml +8/−2
  • Diff: 69467c2
  • Discussion: #3585956 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

MCP resource content cached for one user could be returned to other users. A resource that varied by a cache context such as user kept serving the first caller's content to everyone with view access until the entry expired. Access checks still ran on every call, so the leak only affected users who were allowed to read the resource. Each caller now gets the cached variation for their own context values.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Cached MCP resource content could be served to a different user than the one it was generated for, when the content varied by cache context (e.g. user) and both users had view access.

Technical details

The old ResourceContentCache::generate() stored the first caller's resolved context keys (for example [user]=10) in a pointer entry at mcp_resource:{uri}. It reused that suffix for every later lookup. Render caching avoids this by storing context tokens and resolving them again on each request.

The class now delegates storage to core's VariationCacheInterface, the store RenderCache uses. It is wired as a new service, mcp_server.variation_cache.resource, created from variation_cache_factory over the default bin. The mcp_server.resource_content_cache service takes only that service as its argument, so the constructor no longer takes cache.default and cache_contexts_manager. Cache keys are ['mcp_resource', hash('sha256', $expandedUri)]. The URI is hashed because it is client-controlled and the variation cache joins keys and context keys with :, so a raw URI could spell another caller's cache ID. The access result's cacheability is passed as the initial cacheability to both get() and set(), and it is merged into the DTO metadata.

Behavior that stays the same: the access callback runs on every call and is never cached, and a NULL from the content callback raises ResourceNotFoundException. Content with max-age 0 is not stored. A new kernel test, ResourceContentCacheTest, covers two users reading one resource, the URI-spoofing case, and max-age 0.

Upgrade

Previously cached resource content sits under the old mcp_resource:{uri} pointer keys, which the new code does not read, so it is simply ignored. Clear caches if you want those stale entries removed. Code that constructs ResourceContentCache directly must pass a VariationCacheInterface instead of the cache backend and contexts manager. The class is final and used through the mcp_server.resource_content_cache service.

Summary

When the MCP server runs over STDIO (drush mcp:server), content edits made by an AI client were stamped with the time the client connected, not the time of the edit. This affected entity changed times, revision creation times and comment created times. Each STDIO message now gets the current time as its request time, so timestamps are correct for the whole session. HTTP transport was never affected.

drush mcp:server is one long-lived PHP process, so Drupal's request time, read from the initial request's REQUEST_TIME, never advanced. It subscribes to the MCP SDK's Mcp\Event\RequestEvent at priority 1000, so other listeners already see the new time.

When PHP_SAPI === 'cli', it sets REQUEST_TIME and REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT on the current request's server bag. It also sets them in $_SERVER, because core's time service falls back to $_SERVER when there is no request. Under any other SAPI it does nothing, since each HTTP message is already its own request. item.title: #3585955: Concurrent requests on one session get 503 "MCP session lock timeout" after a lost lock race
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +271/−9 · php +267/−6 · md +3/−3 · yml +1
  • Diff: 65bce47
  • Discussion: #3585955 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

When an MCP client sent several requests at once on the same session (for example resources/read, resources/list and tools/list), some of them could fail immediately with a 503 "MCP session lock timeout" even though no real timeout had happened. Requests that lose the race for the session lock now keep waiting, up to 30 seconds in total, and only get a 503 if the lock really stays busy that long. The reporter's test went from 2 failures in 90 requests to 270 of 270 passing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: LockBackendSessionLock takes the datetime.time service as a new third constructor argument.

Technical details

LockBackendInterface::wait() returns as soon as the lock looks free. With three or more concurrent requests, two waiters can see it free, one takes it, and the other's single follow-up acquire() fails at once. LockBackendSessionLock::acquire() now loops on acquire() against one deadline of WAIT_SECONDS (30), computed from TimeInterface::getCurrentMicroTime(). Each wait() gets only the remaining time, rounded up to whole seconds. A TRUE return from wait() means the lock stayed held for the whole delay, so it throws SessionLockTimeoutException, which the SDK answers with a 503. A FALSE return means the lock looked free, so the loop retries acquire(). Retrying acquire() once more was rejected because it only moves the race. Restarting a full 30 s wait() each time was rejected because it could hold a worker without limit.

The loop lives in LockBackendSessionLock, the SessionLockInterface adapter the SDK calls for every locked request. The issue says an earlier patch with a separate SessionLock class was dropped in favor of this. The service definition gains @datetime.time as a third argument. The commit adds unit tests (LockBackendSessionLockRaceTest, with FakeClock and ContendedLockBackend helpers) covering a free lock, lost races, a shared budget and a long hold. The kernel test constructors were updated for the new argument.

Upgrade

Rebuild caches after updating, because the mcp_server.session_lock service definition gained an argument. Code that constructs LockBackendSessionLock directly must pass the time service as the third argument:

new LockBackendSessionLock($lock, $database, $this->container->get('datetime.time'))

item.title: #3586769: Full chat thread pool deletes the conversation in slot 0 on every new thread and carries over previous conversation context
item.description:

For AI assistants using the private_tempstore_pool chat history mode, once a user had 11 open threads (for example by refreshing the chatbot page instead of using Clear History), every chat request deleted their conversation in slot 0. The evicted key is also removed from the runner's temp store (getTempStore()->delete($evicted_key)), so output_contexts and structured_results from the previous conversation no longer carry over. item.title: #3585954: Replace SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport with the SDK's session lock
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +665/−550 · php +629/−515 · md +26/−23 · yml +9/−11 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 41b50f6
  • Discussion: #3585954 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

mcp_server 2.x now requires mcp/sdk 0.9 or later, and drops support for 0.7 and 0.8. Per-session request serialization is no longer done by module code in the HTTP controller and a custom transport. The SDK's own session lock now does it, backed by Drupal's lock service. The change also fixes tool input schemas that Tool API writes with an empty properties map (an \ArrayObject), which the SDK's Tool class would not accept.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: mcp/sdk constraint changed from ^0.7.1 || ^0.8 to ^0.9; 0.7 and 0.8 are no longer supported.
  • API change: The mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service (tagged mcp_server.transport_middleware) is removed. McpServerController no longer takes the lock or database services.
  • New API: New mcp_server.session_lock service, Drupal\mcp_server\Session\LockBackendSessionLock, implementing the SDK's SessionLockInterface.

Technical details

McpServerFactory takes a new SessionLockInterface argument and passes it to Builder::setSessionLock(). The implementation is LockBackendSessionLock, registered as mcp_server.session_lock with the lock and database services. It keeps the lock name mcp_session:<sha256 of session id>. acquire() waits once and then throws the SDK's SessionLockTimeoutException. tryAcquire() is for the SDK's SSE polls. release() is deferred while Connection::inTransaction() is true, because a rollback would restore the deleted semaphore row. This keeps the old behavior for a tool that suspends inside a transaction.

SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport, which overrode protected SDK hooks, is deleted. So are its lock handling in McpServerController::handle() and the PassThroughMiddleware class. The controller now builds the SDK's StreamableHttpTransport and passes the SDK's PassthroughMiddleware when no middleware is tagged. SSE responses are still converted to streamed Symfony responses. A lock timeout is now answered by the SDK (503 with a JSON-RPC error), not by ServiceUnavailableHttpException.

The 0.7/0.8 compatibility code is also removed. That covers the method_exists() guards around setRequestState(), McpServerServiceProvider::alter(), and the mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service. FiberShield now recognizes the SDK's RequestSuspension and NotificationSuspension objects, where it used to look for an array with a type key. McpServerFactory converts an \ArrayObject schema map to an array. A test_array_object_input tool was added to mcp_server_test to cover that. The CI lowest-SDK job and the contributor docs now pin ^0.9.

Upgrade

Update the constraint in composer.json:

"mcp/sdk": "^0.9"

Code that tags or references mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version, or constructs McpServerController directly with the lock and database arguments, needs updating. The SDK's transport already applies ProtocolVersionMiddleware to handshake-era requests.
